about: Blackout's base rates from EAGLE-I's outage history: how often each state had more than each line of customers out for an hour or more, built by tools/eaglei_history.py (see blackout/eaglei.py for the rule). Not a live feed; rebuilt by hand when figshare adds a year.
citation: Brelsford, C., Tennille, S., Myers, A., Chinthavali, S., Tansakul, V., Denman, M., et al. The Environment for Analysis of Geo-Located Energy Information's Recorded Electricity Outages 2014-2025. figshare, dataset (2023, version 4 of 25 Feb 2026). https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.24237376
rule: A state's total is the sum of its counties' customers_out in a 15-minute run (UTC). A run where any of its counties shows more than 100,000 customers out beyond 1.1 times EAGLE-I's modelled customers for it (MCC.csv, 2022) is suspect for that state: kept, but it can't make an episode by itself or set its peak. Runs missing from the file are unknown and neither join nor split. An episode is readings above the line with no more than 3 known readings under it between them and no more than 6 hours from one to the next, 4 or more of them not suspect; it counts in the month and year it starts. Its hours run from its first reading to the end of its last; its peak is the highest total held over 4 readings in a row that aren't suspect.
